citations.quote: The Applicant has demonstrated efficacy of eplontersen for the treatment of hATTR-PN in Study ION-682884-CS3.
The efficacy of WAINUA was demonstrated in a randomized, open-label, multicenter clinical trial in adult patients with polyneuropathy caused by hATTR amyloidosis (Study 1; NCT04136184).

Effectiveness and safety were assessed by evaluating the results from the Phase 3, randomized, open-label, active comparator, and externally controlled ION-682884-CS3 study in adult subjects with hATTR-PN.

design.text: Randomized, open-label, multicenter study of eplontersen (45 mg every 4 weeks) using inotersen as an active control, with efficacy assessed against an external placebo group from another study (NCT01737398).

citations.quote: Study ION-682884-CS3 is a randomized, open-label study of eplontersen (45 mg given every 4 weeks) in adult patients with hATTR-PN using inotersen as an active control.

Efficacy assessments were based on a comparison of the WAINUA arm of Study 1 with an external placebo group (N=60) in another study (NCT01737398) composed of a comparable population of adult patients with polyneuropathy caused by hATTR amyloidosis.

population.text: Adult subjects with stage 1 or stage 2 hATTR-PN with documented genetic mutation in the TTR gene and NIS of 10 to 130 at baseline.

citations.quote: ION-682884-CS3	Subjects with stage 1 or stage 2 hATTR-PN with documented genetic mutation in the TTR gene and NIS of 10 to 130 at baseline

endpoint.text: The efficacy endpoints were change from baseline to Week 35 in the modified Neuropathy Impairment Score +7 (mNIS+7) composite score and change from baseline to Week 35 in the Norfolk Quality of Life-Diabetic Neuropathy (QoL-DN) total score; change from baseline in serum TTR concentration was also assessed.

citations.quote: The primary efficacy objective was to study the efficacy of eplontersen as compared with the external control of the placebo cohort in the ISIS-420915-CS2 study, evaluating change from baseline in the modified Neuropathy Impairment Score +7 (mNIS+7) and change from baseline in serum TTR concentration.

The efficacy endpoints were the change from baseline to Week 35 in the modified Neuropathy Impairment Scale+7 (mNIS+7) composite score and the change from baseline to Week 35 in the Norfolk Quality of Life-Diabetic Neuropathy (QoL-DN) total score.

n.text: 144 subjects randomized to eplontersen, 24 to concurrent inotersen, and 60 in the external placebo group.

citations.quote: Study CS3 included 144 subjects randomized to the eplontersen arm, 24 to the concurrent inotersen arm, and 60 in the external placebo group.

result.text: At Week 35, mNIS+7 change from baseline was 0.2 (WAINUA) vs 9.2 (placebo), treatment difference LS Mean -9.0 (95% CI -13.5, -4.5), p<0.001; Norfolk QoL-DN change was -3.1 vs 8.7, treatment difference -11.8 (95% CI -16.8, -6.8), p<0.001.

citations.quote: Treatment with WAINUA resulted in statistically significant improvements in the mNIS+7 and the Norfolk QoL-DN total scores, compared to the external placebo control (p<0.001) at Week 35 (Table 2, Figures 1 and 3). The distributions of changes in mNIS+7 and Norfolk QoL-DN scores from baseline to Week 35 by percent of patients in each category are shown in Figure 2 and Figure 4, respectively.

indication.text: WAINUA is indicated for the treatment of the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults.

citations.quote: WAINUA is indicated for the treatment of the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults.

target_moa.text: Eplontersen is a transthyretin-directed antisense oligonucleotide-GalNAc conjugate that causes hepatic-targeted degradation of mutant and wild-type TTR mRNA through direct binding, reducing serum TTR protein and TTR deposits in tissues.

citations.quote: Eplontersen is an antisense oligonucleotide N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) conjugate that causes hepatic-targeted degradation of TTR mRNA (for mutant variants and wild-type TTR) through direct binding to the TTR mRNA, which results in a reduction of serum TTR protein and TTR protein deposits in tissues.
Established pharmacologic class (EPC)	Transthyretin-directed antisense oligonucleotide

Eplontersen (ION-682884) is a 20-mer chimeric 2'-MOE mixed (PS/PO) backbone ASO conjugated to a triantennary N-acetyl galactosamine (GalNAc3) ligand, which is intended to promote uptake by hepatocytes through recognition by the asialoglycoprotein receptors (ASGPR).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥9% of patients) were vitamin A decreased (15%) and vomiting (9%); other reactions reported in at least 5% of patients included proteinuria (8%), injection site reactions (7%), and blurred vision (6%). Three serious adverse reactions of atrioventricular (AV) heart block (2%) occurred, including 1 case of complete AV block.

detail.text: No boxed warning; FDA concurred that eplontersen would not require a Boxed Warning for thrombocytopenia or glomerulonephritis given the absence of empirical evidence suggesting increased risk.

citations.quote: Based on these findings, the Agency concurs with the Applicant that, if approved, eplontersen would not require a REMS program for thrombocytopenia or glomerulonephritis, and the Applicant's proposal to not include a Boxed Warning or Warnings and Precautions statements for these events in labeling given the absence of empirical evidence suggesting increased risk.
